clue.text: Put in a little extra, say, to one's present

indicators.note: say tells the solver to judge the phrase by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: to put in a little extra is to add some

explanation.surface: Someone tops up a gift for a person, adding a little more to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'present' looks like a gift, but ADSUM is Latin for 'I am present', the reply at a school roll call.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word is the traditional answer when a register is called, declaring that the speaker is here.

clue.text: Similar to a loan badly needed to go to America

indicators.note: badly signals the words a loan are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
US is the United States

explanation.surface: Someone desperately needs a loan to travel to America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly needed' looks like one phrase, but 'badly' scrambles A LOAN into ANALO.
explanation.definitionFit: Analogous things correspond or are alike in some respect.

clue.text: About 101, he may still be a younger member of the family

definitions.text: About 101, he may still be a younger member of the family

indicators.note: About means the son wraps round the Roman numeral

parts.note: a son is a younger member of the family
101 in Roman numerals is CI

explanation.surface: Even at 101, a man can still be the junior of his family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like 'roughly', but it is the container signal; the whole clue, read as one sentence, also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scion is a descendant or heir of a family, especially a young one.

clue.text: Girl grabs one titular head concerning finance

indicators.note: grabs means the girl's name holds the other letters

parts.note: Mary is a girl's name

indicators.note: head means the first letter of titular

explanation.surface: A girl seizes an honorary leader for money matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Monetary describes money and currency, matters of finance.

clue.text: Artisan in boat's crew

parts.note: a boat is a craft, so boat's gives craft's
to crew a vessel is to man it

explanation.surface: A skilled worker serves among the hands on a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a skilled worker who makes things by hand; they are synonyms.

clue.text: The ship's company exulted

definitions.meaning: the people working on a ship
past tense of crow, to boast or gloat, in its old form

explanation.surface: The sailors celebrated triumphantly.
explanation.definitionFit: One word means the sailors manning a vessel and the old past tense of crow, gloated.

clue.text: Fuel change needed in that race

indicators.note: change needed says the letters of the words in that race must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A competition requires a different fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthracite is hard coal, burnt as a smokeless fuel.

clue.text: There's a limit in the attempt to be fashionable

indicators.note: in puts the limit inside the attempt

parts.note: a try is an attempt
an end is a limit

explanation.surface: Trying to be in fashion has its limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trendy follows the latest style, being modish or in vogue.

clue.text: Has suspicions? Have confidence in the girl

indicators.note: in puts confidence inside the girl

parts.note: miss is a girl or young woman
to have confidence is to trust

explanation.surface: Doubts arise, so you're urged to put faith in the young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who distrusts others harbours doubts about them.

clue.text: Many long for a bit of this material

indicators.note: for a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Lots of people yearn for a scrap of this cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylon is a synthetic fibre made into fabric.

clue.text: Lamenting rupture of the alliance

indicators.note: a rupture breaks the word lamenting apart so its letters can be rebuilt

explanation.surface: Someone mourns the break-up of a partnership between nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Nations in alignment are lined up together, which is a synonym for being in a formal pact.

clue.text: Support moving money to end of property contract

indicators.note: moving, together with the words 'to end of', says one letter shifts to the back of the contract word

parts.note: a lease is a contract for renting property
L stands for pound (libra), the British unit of money

explanation.surface: Money changes hands to complete a deal over a house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' with 'to end of' takes the L of LEASE to the back, giving EASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's stand that holds up a canvas is a frame of support.

clue.text: Sailors consumed with love at first — fancy!

indicators.note: at first places the letter for love at the front, before the sailors

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written O
RN is the Royal Navy, a crossword stock for sailors
consumed means ate

explanation.surface: Sailors are gripped by love at first sight, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy!' looks like an exclamation, but it is the adjective meaning elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborately decorated is showy and elaborate, the adjectival sense of fancy.

clue.text: Distribution system by club in US football field

parts.note: the grid is the network distributing electricity
an iron is a type of golf club

explanation.surface: A power network sits beside a club on an American sports pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The pitch in American football is nicknamed for its parallel marked lines, like a cooking grill.

clue.text: One of 21, say, has a friend in copper with capital

parts.note: a pal is a friend
taken as written
D is the old British penny, a copper coin
Rome is the Italian capital

explanation.surface: Someone has a friend in the police and money to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is TENETS, which reads the same backwards. 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the old penny, D.
explanation.definitionFit: A word reading the same forwards and backwards is the kind 21 down is an example of.

clue.text: Ritual involving even cobras

indicators.note: involving is read as making something involved, so the letters of the words even cobras are tangled

explanation.surface: A ceremony in which snakes play a part.
explanation.definitionFit: A religious observance is a rite or customary practice kept by worshippers.

clue.text: Boy and girl in an unpaid sort of caring organisation

parts.note: Sam is a boy's name

indicators.note: in places the girl inside an

parts.note: taken as written
Rita is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A young couple volunteer with a charity.
explanation.walkthrough: The Samaritans is a British volunteer charity offering a phone line to people in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: A Good Samaritan helps strangers for nothing, the namesake of the volunteer helpline charity.

clue.text: Accustomed to being exploited

definitions.meaning: taken advantage of by another person

explanation.surface: Someone has grown resigned to being taken advantage of.
explanation.definitionFit: One word covers both being familiar with a habit and being taken advantage of.

clue.text: Finding a bay in Australia

definitions.meaning: ... Bay lies on the coast of Victoria

explanation.surface: Someone stumbles upon an inlet on the Australian coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a thing found, and also names a bay on Victoria's coast.

clue.text: Politician for whom Tom cared terribly

indicators.note: terribly signals the words Tom cared are mangled

explanation.surface: Tom was deeply devoted to a particular statesman.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US party opposed to the Republicans is an American politician.

clue.text: Prophet knocks back drink? On the contrary

indicators.note: knocks back is read literally as turning the prophet's name backwards

parts.note: Amos is an Old Testament prophet

explanation.surface: A prophet downs a drink, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the surface: it is the drink (SOMA) that is the prophet knocked back, not the prophet doing the drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Soma is the ritual intoxicating beverage of Vedic India, and also the drug in Brave New World.

clue.text: Ruffles a girl's hair

parts.note: Di, short for Diana, is a girl's name, so a girl's gives Di's
tresses are long locks of hair

explanation.surface: Someone messes up a young woman's hairdo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruffles' looks like the verb for mussing hair, but the definition means upsets.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle someone is to upset or trouble them, which is what distresses does.

clue.text: Code of morals when 'e's in camp

indicators.note: in places the letter inside the camp

parts.note: a camp is made up of tents
'e is he with the h dropped, so it is just E

explanation.surface: A Cockney asks about ethics while he is under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenets are principles or doctrines held as true, together a moral code.

clue.text: Gives warning of the drinks being about to run out

indicators.note: being about means the drinks word wraps around the next piece

parts.note: ports are fortified wines
to run out is to end

explanation.surface: A host warns that the bar is about to run dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To portend is to foreshadow or signal something coming, often trouble.

clue.text: Old king takes boat round the island

indicators.note: round means the boat goes round the island

parts.note: a pram is a small flat-bottomed dinghy
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An ancient ruler sails around an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boat' is not a baby carriage here: a pram is also a dinghy. Priam was the king of Troy in Greek legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Priam was the last king of Troy in Homer's Iliad.

clue.text: The French have a right to jeer about this jacket

indicators.note: about says the jeer goes round the other letters

parts.note: to jeer is to boo
le is French for the

explanation.surface: French people are entitled to mock a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bolero is a short open jacket ending above the waist, from Spanish dress.

clue.text: Priest rising to poet

parts.note: Eli was a priest in the Bible, mentor of Samuel

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word to is read upwards, backwards

explanation.surface: A clergyman is promoted to bard.
explanation.definitionFit: T S Eliot was an American-born British poet, author of The Waste Land.

clue.text: Why include eggs initially in Miss Muffet's diet?

indicators.note: include means the word why takes in the next letter

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of eggs

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about eggs in a nursery-rhyme girl's meals.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Miss Muffet, in the English nursery rhyme, sat on a tuffet eating her curds and whey.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin liquid left after milk curdles is what the rhyme's girl ate with her curds.

clue.text: Communication omitting record of fibre

indicators.note: omitting means the record is left out of the communication

parts.note: an epistle is a letter
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A message leaves out an account of a material.
explanation.definitionFit: Istle is a plant fibre from Mexican agave or yucca, used for cord and brushes.

clue.text: "He'd have acted ____ if he had been acuter" (Gilbert)

definitions.text: "He'd have acted ____ if he had been acuter" (Gilbert)

parts.words: "He'd have acted ____ if he had been acuter" (Gilbert)
parts.note: a quotation from W S Gilbert's comic opera lyrics with a word missing; the solver supplies the word meaning differently

explanation.surface: A line of Gilbert's verse with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a blank after 'acted'; the word that fills it rhymes with 'acuter' in Gilbert's patter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in another way, differently from how one did, fills the gap in the quoted line.

clue.text: Order home

parts.note: read as the house where members of a religious order live, not a command to go back

explanation.definitionFit: Monks of a religious order live together in such a building.

clue.text: Matting remains dry when immersed in the river

indicators.note: immersed in places the dry letters inside the river

parts.note: the Tay is a Scottish river
TT means teetotal, abstaining from alcohol

explanation.surface: A mat stays dry even when dipped in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tay is the longest river in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A tatty is a mat of woven grass, hung wet in Indian doorways to cool the air.
